previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 20%), COPD, type I diabetes, and prior crack cocaine use was admitted for acute on chronic systolic heart failure triggered by dietary sodium indiscretion. He presented with progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, and cough with frothy sputum. Initial evaluation revealed hypoxia, elevated BNP, and bilateral pulmonary opacities on imaging. He was treated with IV furosemide for aggressive diuresis, resulting in a weight loss from 201 to 193 lbs. Due to persistent respiratory distress, he was briefly monitored in the ICU but did not require mechanical ventilation. Antibiotics and steroids were discontinued after no evidence of infection or acute pneumonitis was found. His carvedilol was reduced due to blood pressure concerns, and lasix was increased to 40 mg twice daily at discharge. He improved clinically, ambulating independently on room air, and was discharged home with instructions on daily weight monitoring, low-sodium diet, and follow-up for cardiology and hepatitis C management.

# Actue on chronic Systolic CHF exacerbation: Patient presented 
with respiratory distress, noted to be tachypneic with O2 
saturation of 82% on room air initially, which improved back to 
baseline with diuresis (lasix gtt). He had a history of crack 
pneumonitis and systolic congestive heart failure, as well as a 
diagnosis of COPD. Possible etiologies of the patient's 
exacerbation included pneumonitis from continued crack use, 
heart failure exacerbation or COPD exacerbation.  Given his 
orthopnea, PND, and possible underdosing of his furosemide, pt 
was diuresed with a lasix gtt with a large symptomatic 
improvement.  His breathing appeared back to baseline after 
agressive diuresis with lasix gtt in the ICU.  After being 
called out to them edical floor pt was restarted on his home 
dose of po lasix 40 mg bid.  He was also continued on his 
ipratropium and albuterol nebs, as well as 
fluticasone/salmeterol.  He was also continued on carvidelol and 
lisinopril for sCHF.
  
# Type I Diabetes:  Pt's BG's were in the 400's initially in the 
ICU, likely ___ to the high dose steroids he received in the ED. 
 Once on the medical floor his BG's remained in the low 200's 
before discharge.  He will follow up with his PCP for further 
titration of his insulin.

# Schizophrenia: Patient was not currently on antipsychotics and 
was scheduled to see a psychiatrist this week. He reports 
continuously hearing voices, oftentimes telling him to hurt 
himself. He has never acted on these voices, and has no current 
suicidal or homicidal ideation. Psychiatry was consulted and 
recommended outpt follow up.
